thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SEV2 - streaming tail latency spike detected for /v1/stream (eu-west-1). p95 ~ 1.2s, p99 observed spikes up to 12.4s. Overall SLO breaches starting 2026-03-14T08:07Z. @Ryan you are on-call
Ryan: Ack. Paging in. Looking at dashboards now — which fleet / model?
Maya: I see correlated errors in the quant-runner logs for model=llm-large-1 with precision-profile=prec-v2-int8-calib. Heap of dequant stalls and repeated KV cache misses.
Anika: Can we confirm whether this is only in eu-west-1 or global?
Josh: Metrics show eu-west1 and eu-central1 hot, na not affected. Top traffic is streaming chat sessions -> heavy short-sequence streams (lots of small requests). Batching profile changed yesterday with the precision rollout.
infra-bot: autoscaler: current pool usage gpu-pool-eu: 85% -> scale_target 140%. New nodes provisioning (3).
Ryan: Good. Initial hypothesis: recent precision-profile rollout (prec-v2-int8-calib) introduced slower dequant kernels under streaming + KV cache pattern, causing tail latency. Need quick mitigation to restore SLO.
Maya: Quick mitigations we can do now: 1) Route streaming traffic to fallback fp16/legacy-quant model variant 2) Rollback precision-profile rollout 3) Temporarily reduce batching window to avoid large build-ups. Which is fastest?
Josh: Routing is fastest (policy change). Rollback of profile requires a coordinated config rollback across infra and may need a restart - takes longer. Reducing batching window is infra change but doable.
Anika: I'll update routing policy to prefer model variant llm-large-1-fp16 for requests with header `x-mode: streaming` in eu regions. That should divert ~70% of streaming requests.
Ricardo: I'll prepare the rollback command and test plan if we need it: `infractl deploy rollback --service=precision-controller --tag=prec-v1` then `runtimectl restart-model llm-large-1 --graceful`.
Emily: We should notify impacted customers as we mitigate. I have a support ticket from AcmeSearch reporting noticeable stalls in the EU region (ticket #ACME-4521).
support-alex: Confirmed. AcmeSearch sees >10s stalls on the bot replies. They're on dedicated capacity but routing through hosted model pool because of a recent failover. Customer impact: degraded UX, potential SLA violation for their paid plan.
incident-bot: Incident severity escalated to SEV2 -> Notify PM, Customer Success, and Legal. Postmortem required.
Ryan: Action plan: 1) Anika change routing now 2) Maya reduce batching window to 10ms (from 50ms) for eu streaming queues 3) Ricardo stage rollback but hold unless routing + batching don't restore p99 < 2s 4) Emily draft customer-facing status, support-alex hold off pushing until we have confirmation of improvement
Maya: Applying batching window change: setting `runtime.streaming.batch_window_ms=10` for queue eu-stream-01.
Maya: Done — change applied, no restart required.
Anika: Routing policy update done: preferring llm-large-1-fp16 for header `x-mode: streaming` in eu. Will take effect within 20s.
Ryan: Watching dashboards — p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 350ms within 40s, p99 dropping from 12.4s -> 2.8s. Good sign.
Josh: Log snippet from quant-runner prior to mitigation:
```
E 08:06:22 quant_runner.cpp:491 dequant_kernel: slow path triggered, elapsed_ms=82
W 08:06:22 kv_cache.cpp:213 miss_count=1243, miss_latency_ms=48
E 08:06:23 server_stream.cpp:117 stall_detected session=abcd-1234 stall_ms=12004
```
Maya: After routing change we see fewer calls to quant-runner for streaming - counts down 68%.
Ricardo: Given improvement, I'm going to hold rollback. Preparing rollback playbook anyway in case p99 spikes back.
Emily: Draft status for AcmeSearch: "We are aware of intermittent streaming stalls in EU; mitigation in progress — routing to a fallback model variant and config changes have reduced latency. We will follow up with postmortem." Want to confirm wording.
support-alex: Fine, send once Ryan or I ack. Keep it calm and mention ETA for follow-up 4 hours.
Ryan: Agreed. Sending now.
Ryan: Sending internal note to PM and CS with summary and links.
infra-bot: scale action completed: 3 nodes added to gpu-pool-eu, pool capacity +18%.
Josh: Noticed one customer-specific anomaly: AcmeSearch traffic pattern was high QPS of many short streaming sessions which exacerbated dequant stalls. Might be a workload sensitivity to quant profile.
Anika: Trace samples show dequant hot path more likely when KV cache has many small segments. fp16 variant avoids dequant entirely — explains quicker recovery.
Maya: We're still seeing occasional streaming stalls at p99 ~2.0s; under target of <1.5s. Next steps: consider rolling back prec-v2-int8-calib if p99 doesn't go under 1.5s in next 30 minutes. Also run calibration validation suite on a staging workload that mirrors short streaming sessions.
Ricardo: Rollback readiness checklist: config snapshot, run smoke tests, schedule low-impact window. I can trigger a rollback in ~12 minutes if needed.
Ryan: I'll stay on the thread for handoff. Maya — can you take this through the next 2 hours? I'll hand off to you at 08:30Z.
Maya: Taking over. Summary for handoff: cause suspected precision-profile prec-v2-int8-calib introduced slower dequant kernels under streaming/KV cache pattern -> tail latency spike in EU. Mitigations applied: routing to fp16 variant, reduced batching window, scaled pool. Current state: p95 ~320ms, p99 ~1.9s, customer notification sent.
Ryan: Thanks. I'm leaving notes in postmortem template and capturing log pointers. @Emily please own the customer followup and coordinate the postmortem.
Emily: Will do. I'll collect evals and perf diffs, include calibration test outputs.
Anika: I'll start a staging run that reproduces streaming short-seq workload against both prec-v1 and prec-v2 to capture perf delta.
Josh: Recommended long-term: add canary loadshape for streaming short-seq traffic when rolling out precision profiles; add perf gates on p99 for streaming endpoints and automated rollback trigger.
Maya: Agreed. Adding to postmortem action items: canary + perf gate + more granular kernel telemetry for dequant paths.
incident-bot: SEV2 -> monitoring in progress. Next update in 15 minutes or on major state change.
Ryan: Handing off. I'm out for pager rotation shift. Maya has the lead.
Maya: Acknowledged, running checks and will escalate to rollback if p99 >=2.5s again.
Ricardo: Documented rollback steps in `#runbooks/precision-rollbacks` and flagged owners.
support-alex: Keeping AcmeSearch ticket open and will update them at +1h if stable.
Emily: Capturing artifacts for postmortem: perf graphs, quant-runner traces, routing change diff, batching config diff, customer ticket IDs.
Maya: Closing current mitigation loop: observed sustained p99 < 2s for last 8 minutes. Keeping monitor alarms tightened. Will update thread with final status and write postmortem stub.
incident-bot: Incident note: mitigated, but not resolved. Postmortem required.
Maya: Final note before I start postmortem draft: root cause hypothesis: prec-v2-int8-calib changed kernel selection that under short streaming & high KV fragmentation paths forces dequant slow path -> tail stalls. Action items: rollback guard rails, canaries, perf gates, customer comms.
Emily: I'll coordinate the postmortem and assign owners.
Maya: Thanks team. If p99 regresses, ping me directly.
Ryan: Thanks everyone. Leaving channel.
